prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every car wreck — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, how badly you were hurt, whether there are complicated liability or insurance issues, and how you like to work with your lawyer. I can help you find a great lawyer for your case; here’s how to choose one and steps to take right now.

Key qualifications to look for
- Focused experience in Texas car-accident/personal-injury law (not primarily family law, estate planning, etc.).  
- Trial experience and a record of negotiating sizable settlements and verdicts.  
- Experience handling cases with similar facts (T-bone, rear-end, commercial vehicle, catastrophic injury, wrongful death, uninsured motorist, etc.).  
- Willingness to take the case on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Typical contingency fees in Texas are about 33%–40% plus costs.  
- Good communication: returns calls/emails, explains strategy, provides a point of contact.  
- Resources: investigators, medical experts, accident-reconstruction experts if needed.  
- Clean disciplinary record with the State Bar of Texas.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Houston Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service (search “Houston Bar lawyer referral”).  
- Texas State Bar website: verify license and disciplinary history.  
- National and local lawyer directories: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers — use them as a starting point, but read underlying reviews and outcomes.  
- Google Maps and Yelp for recent client reviews.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident/personal-injury cases have you handled in Harris County?  
- How many of those went to trial vs. settled? Can you share examples or results (client names redacted)?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day? Will junior associates or paralegals do most of the work?  
- Do you take cases on contingency? What percentage and what costs are deducted?  
- What is your initial assessment of liability and value in my case? What evidence is needed?  
- How long do you expect the case to take?  
- How often will you update me and by what method?

Red flags
- Promises of a specific recovery amount or guaranteed outcome.  
- Pressure to sign immediately or vague fee arrangements.  
- Poor communication during the initial contact.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of Houston firms/lawyers to call if you tell me your ZIP code and a few case facts (severity of injuries, whether the other driver had insurance, whether a commercial vehicle was involved).  
- Draft a short script or email you can use to contact lawyers for consultations.

Which would you prefer: help narrowing to several attorneys near you, or a checklist/script to use when you call?
